question: What first made pop songs about three minutes long?
answer: The grain of shellac. Songs were first cut on 78s, pressed from a gritty, noisy shellac mix that needed a wide groove and a fast spin, so a 10-inch side ran out after about three minutes. Vinyl's finer grain made the 20-minute LP side possible in 1948, but singles and radio had already fixed the shape.
move: When a habit has no reason today, look for the machine it was built for.
ask: Which of my habits was shaped by a machine I no longer use?

start.text: Most pop songs still end at around three minutes.

levels.text: Radio and the 7-inch single kept songs that length for decades.
They took it from the 10-inch 78, the disc songs were first cut for.
A 78 spun fast in a wide groove, so each side ran out quickly.
Gritty shellac couldn't hold the fine groove vinyl later could.

reference: Mark Katz, Capturing Sound: How Technology Has Changed Music, University of California Press, 2004, ch. 1
